author: Isabel Martin
title: Greenville County Sheriff's Office introduces new policies after training exercise shooting - NewsBreak
text:
By Isabel Martin ,
7 hours ago
GREENVILLE COUNTY, S.C. (WSPA) — The Greenville County Sheriff’s Office is introducing new safety practices after two deputies were shot during a SWAT training exercise in July.
The incident occurred inside a vacant building at 2000 Wade Hampton Boulevard on July 29 . The pair were hit by a breaching round from a shotgun.
The deputies were hospitalized and one deputy underwent surgery, officials said. One deputy has since returned to work on a “light-duty status,” while the other is still recovering from his injuries.
SWAT Training Incident Sheriff Hobart Lewis explained what led up to the shooting during a press conference on August 6 .
While preparing for a training scenario, one deputy was tasked with getting blank 12-gauge shotgun rounds. The deputy, along with another deputy assigned to the training center, acquired a “baggie” of breaching rounds, which are normally used to break through windows or doors.
Believing the rounds were blank simulation ammunition, Lewis said the deputies tested the rounds by firing them into a berm that was too far away to properly ensure the rounds were blanks.
During the press conference, Lewis clarified all ammunition used by deputies is supposed to be kept in an armory maintained by the Greenville County Sheriff’s Office. Additionally, the office’s live and simulation ammunition are normally kept separate from one another and are clearly marked.
When the scenario began, another deputy, playing the role of an armed individual, fired one of the breaching rounds at deputies, striking two.
Once the deputies realized they were bleeding, Lewis said they ended the scenario immediately.
What are the new training policies for the sheriff’s office? The sheriff’s office said the new practices are an effort to prevent a similar incident from occurring in the future.
Ammunition Storage Going forward, the Greenville County Sheriff’s Office said that all ammunition will be stored separately in labeled containers. With the exception of during active training sessions, loose ammunition is prohibited from being stored in desks, offices, the range house or classrooms.
Post-Training Disposal The sheriff’s office has also introduced an ammunition post-training disposal policy, meaning that any ammunition issues to those involved in training must be returned to the office’s Training Center Lieutenant to ensure proper disposal.
Simunition (SIMS) Equipment All simulated ammunition, or simunition equipment will only be given to SIMS-certified instructors by training center staff. All gear must be returned to staff at the end of training.
Use of Blank Ammunition The policy mandates that all blanks must be fired from a SIMS weapon, blank-only weapon, or a firearm with a SIMS bolt. Weapons must be triple-checked (self-check, buddy check and safety officer check) before use.
Controlled Storage Policy All gear will be stored at the Center for Advanced Training (CAT). Equipment should be returned to CAT staff within five working days after the training.
Training Plans & Approval Training plans must be approved by a Major at least five days before the exercise. The SWAT Team Commander is in charge of planning, safety oversight, execution and documentation.
Who can participate in training? The sheriff’s office said that volunteers are prohibiting from partaking in training exercises, unless approved by a Major. SWAT members and CAT staff can participate in role-playing exercises. Deputies and civilians attending the training can only observe and are required to high-visibility clothing and protective equipment.
Where can the training take place? If training on a property not owned by Greenville County, a signed training access agreement must be sent to a Major before the training starts.
If training on a county property that is not the CAT, an email from the county employee involved must acknowledge the training and be sent to a Major.
For training exercises held in public spaces or on public property, the sheriff’s office required that efforts be made to alert residents, businesses and organizations in the area.
What’s next? Deputies said the investigation into the shooting is still ongoing. Sheriff Lewis said some disciplinary actions will be taken against those involved in the training incident once the investigation concludes. As of August 6, Lewis said that no disciplinary actions have been taken.
While he investigation is ongoing, officials said no shotguns will be used in trainings.
